description: Rangers is an innovation-driven team passionate about artificial intelligence, space science, and human exploration. We aim to develop a scientifically grounded health monitoring solution that addresses real challenges astronauts face during space missions. By combining NASA research, data analysis, and advanced software engineering, we strive to transform scientific insights into practical, impactful technologies that contribute to safer human space exploration.
summary:
Landing on the Moon or Mars is not the end of a mission—it marks the beginning of a new physical challenge. After prolonged exposure to microgravity, astronauts may experience changes in muscle strength, balance, coordination, and functional movement. These abilities do not necessarily recover at the same rate. Team RANGERS developed RecoveryMap, an interactive recovery-monitoring platform addressing key aspects of NASA's SM-204 research gap. RecoveryMap digitizes specialist-defined recovery plans, tracks daily activities and functional assessments, visualizes differences between strength and movement performance, and generates progress reports. Our core innovation, Recovery Gap, reveals when muscle strength and functional performance change at different rates—differences that a single measurement could overlook. The platform incorporates NASA's CFT70 Earth-based bed-rest analog research to demonstrate the scientific problem, while keeping real research observations separate from clearly labeled synthetic astronaut scenarios.
Our vision is to make post-landing recovery on the Moon and Mars more measurable, transparent, and manageable.
details:
RecoveryMap — Team RANGERS

The Challenge: Landing Is Only the Beginning

A successful landing on the Moon or Mars does not automatically mean that astronauts are physically ready to carry out demanding surface operations. Prolonged exposure to microgravity can affect muscle strength, balance, coordination, and sensorimotor performance. These changes may create challenges when astronauts transition to a planetary gravity environment. NASA's Human Research Roadmap identifies this need through SM-204, which calls for the development and testing of self-administered post-planetary-landing assessment and rehabilitation tools. RecoveryMap is our response to this challenge.

Our Solution

RecoveryMap is an interactive, research-informed recovery-monitoring platform developed by Team RANGERS. It connects six essential functions into a single workflow. Mission Control provides a unified dashboard displaying the recovery phase, daily activities, recent physical measurements, and strength–function trends. Recovery Plan allows specialist-defined rehabilitation plans to be imported, reviewed, and organized into daily schedules, while users can track completed and skipped activities, fatigue, discomfort, and session notes. Functional Assessment records muscle strength, functional movement time, balance, and coordination measurements with dates, units, and baseline references.

At the center of our solution is Recovery Gap, our core innovation, which compares baseline-relative changes in muscle strength and functional movement performance. For example, in a clearly labeled synthetic demonstration, muscle strength is 9% below baseline while functional performance is 23.6% below baseline, creating a difference of 14.6 percentage points. This comparison helps reveal differences between physical strength and functional ability that may be overlooked when evaluating only one metric. Progress & Reports tracks recovery history, session completion, adherence, physical measurements, and observations, with information available for export and specialist review. Finally, NASA Research presents NASA CFT70 Earth-analog research measurements, scientific references, and data provenance separately from fictional astronaut scenarios.

NASA Data and Scientific Foundation

RecoveryMap draws on NASA's CFT70 head-down-bed-rest analog research to investigate differences between physical strength and functional task performance. The platform also references NASA's Functional Task Test research, post-flight reconditioning resources, and the SM-204 research gap. CFT70 participants are Earth-based research participants, not astronauts. Their measurements are not presented as evidence that RecoveryMap has been validated for lunar or Martian deployment.

What Makes RecoveryMap Innovative?

Most activity-tracking systems focus on whether a scheduled exercise was completed. RecoveryMap goes further by connecting three essential questions: What recovery activities were planned? Which activities were actually completed? How did measurable physical performance change? Our Recovery Gap approach makes differences between strength and functional movement visible through transparent, reproducible calculations. Rather than relying on an unexplained clinical risk score, RecoveryMap uses baseline-relative measurements and displays the underlying data. The platform combines specialist-defined plans, daily activity tracking, physical assessments, longitudinal visualization, and research evidence in a mission-oriented interface.

Technology and Development

RecoveryMap is a browser-based application developed using React, TypeScript, and modern web technologies. The platform includes interactive charts, structured document and CSV imports, local data persistence, measurement processing, and report exports. Our source code is hosted on GitHub, and the live application is deployed through Vercel.

Intended Impact

RecoveryMap aims to support the development of more measurable and structured post-landing recovery workflows for future Moon and Mars exploration. With appropriate specialist oversight and further validation, similar systems could help crews document physical changes, follow predefined recovery plans, and communicate progress to medical teams when direct supervision is limited. The same principles may also contribute to remote rehabilitation and physical monitoring applications on Earth.

Our mission is simple: go beyond tracking recovery activities and make recovery itself measurable, understandable, and actionable for human review.
